title: Range and neighbour queries on a sorted set

blocks.text: A `TreeSet` keeps its elements sorted, which makes **range queries** and **neighbour queries** cheap: `subSet(from, fromInclusive, to, toInclusive)`, `ceiling(x)` (the smallest element `>= x`) and `floor(x)` (the largest `<= x`). The page uses them on a set of scores.

items: `new Scoreboard(scores)` keeps each score **once**, as a set does.
`between(low, high)` lists the scores from `low` to `high`, **both ends included**, ascending, as a new list (`low > high` is refused with `IllegalArgumentException`).
`atLeast(x)` is the smallest score `>= x` and `atMost(x)` the largest `<= x`; **an exact match counts**, and when there is none the result is `OptionalInt.empty()`.

cases.says: between(70, 95) includes both 70 and 95, as the page's subSet(70, true, 95, true) does.
atLeast(85) and atMost(85) are both 85, because ceiling and floor include an equal element.
atLeast(101) and atMost(10) are empty, and a range with no scores is an empty list.
A score given twice appears once in a range, as in a set.

concepts: A TreeSet keeps elements sorted and answers range queries with subSet and neighbour queries with ceiling and floor, which include an equal element.
